title: Quantum metric induced nonlinear transport in the hidden loop-current phase of kagome metal RbV$_3$Sb$_5$
authors: Jia-Chen Shi, Shupeng Xu, Utkarsh Khandelwal, Nashra Pistawala, Luminita Harnagea, Steven J. May, Ritesh Agarwal
abstract: A hidden low-temperature phase with possible loop-current order has been proposed in the kagome metals AV$_3$Sb$_5$ (A=K, Rb or Cs), but its experimental signatures remain subtle and indirect. Here, we use third-order nonlinear transport to probe this hidden phase in RbV$_3$Sb$_5$. At ~35 K, the longitudinal cubic response develops a strong kink and pronounced directional anisotropy with a strong departure from common relaxation time scaling, while the transverse cubic response acquires a magnetic field-odd component at the same temperature. Their coincident onset identifies the third-harmonic response as a sensitive marker of the low-temperature electronic reconstruction with time-reversal broken symmetry. Crucially, we find that the quantum metric quadrupole contributes directly to the longitudinal third-order response. In a loop-current charge-density-wave model, its direction selective enhancement captures the observed angular reconstruction. Our work shows how higher-order nonlinear transport translates subtle changes in electronic symmetry and quantum metric into measurable electrical signatures in quantum materials that is important for studying complex electronic phases of matter.
summary: This work uses third-order nonlinear transport measurements to investigate a hidden, low-temperature electronic phase in the kagome metal $	ext{RbV}_3	ext{Sb}_5$. The detection of temperature-dependent kinks and magnetic field-odd components confirms electronic reconstruction and time-reversal symmetry breaking. The analysis attributes the observed directional anisotropy to the quantum metric quadrupole, linking nonlinear transport directly to loop-current order.
main_problem: The study aims to probe a subtle, low-temperature hidden electronic phase, possibly involving loop-current order, in kagome metals.
main_result: The emergence of a field-odd transverse third-harmonic response and a distinct kink in the longitudinal response near 35 K strongly indicate electronic reconstruction and time-reversal symmetry breaking.
method: The research utilizes third-order nonlinear transport measurements ($	ext{V}_{	ext{III}}/	ext{V}_{	ext{I}}^3$) by applying AC electric fields and measuring the resulting third harmonic voltage.
model_or_system: The physical system is the kagome metal $	ext{RbV}_3	ext{Sb}_5$. The theoretical framework involves modeling the low-temperature state using a loop-current charge-density-wave (CDW) model.
key_observables: Third-harmonic response ($	ext{n}=3$), longitudinal and transverse nonlinear coefficients ($	ext{a}_{	ext{III}}, 	ext{a}'_{	ext{III}}$), and the magnetic field-odd component ($	ext{h}'_{	ext{III}}$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), applied magnetic field ($B$), and the angle ($	heta$) of the driving electric field.
main_assumptions: The nonlinear response is successfully decomposed into contributions from the conventional Drude term and the quantum metric quadrupole (QMQ) term.
figures_summary: Figures show the cubic dependence of the third-harmonic voltage on the driving field, the temperature dependence of the nonlinear coefficients highlighting the 35 K kink, and the angular dependence of the response.
paper_structure: The paper establishes third-order nonlinear transport as a sensitive probe, presents measurements showing anomalies at 35 K (longitudinal) and field-odd components (transverse), and finally models the anisotropy using the QMQ contribution within a loop-current CDW framework.
why_interesting: The use of higher-order nonlinear transport to diagnose subtle symmetry breaking (TRSB) and electronic reconstruction in a correlated material like a kagome metal is highly relevant for understanding emergent quantum phases.
